text:
**Short answer:** for the most cells at once, get a 16-bay independent-slot charger. If 8 is enough, the Tenergy TN480U is the only option in these results with a verified price and a direct buy link.

**16 bays (most batteries at once)**
- **Tenergy TN438 (16-bay):** Takes any mix of AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd. It has an LCD showing each cell's status, protection against overcharge, overheating, short circuits and reverse polarity, and an eight-hour timer. [Source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/)
- **BONAI 16-bay:** Any quantity goes in any slot, and AA and AAA can be mixed. It runs on standard 110-240V AC with no separate power brick and delivers 250-500mA per port. Status is shown by LED, with a red flash for a bad cell. [Source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/)
- **POWEROWL 16-bay:** Has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge process (pre-charge, quick, float, trickle). [Source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/)

I didn't get direct purchase links or prices for these three. The review pages only say "Check Price on Amazon" without a usable URL, so I won't guess at links. Searching the product names on Amazon or the brand's store should find them.

**8 bays (cheaper and more compact)**
- **[Tenergy TN480U, $23.99](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger):** This has 8 mixed AA/AAA bays, a per-slot LCD, and negative delta-V termination with bad-cell detection. It charges at 500mA per AA and 250mA per AAA and has a 12-month warranty. The price was verified on 2026-10-21 at [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). The link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.
  - It's USB-C powered, but **no wall adapter is included**, so you need a 5V/2A one. On a 1A source, five or more AA cells drop to 250mA each.
- **EBL 8-bay:** Independent slots with MCU control and per-bay LEDs (red is charging, green is full, flashing red is a bad cell). [Source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/)

**Things to know**
- Most of the independent-slot reviews come from affiliate roundups that read like spec summaries, not hands-on tests. Treat them as feature lists, not proof of performance.
- All of these are for NiMH/NiCd only. Never put alkaline or lithium cells in them.
- With 16 cells at 250-500mA each, expect AA charging to take several hours. Slot independence means one dud cell won't hold up the rest.

If you have 12 or more cells, I'd go with the Tenergy TN438 for its LCD and protections. If you have 8 or fewer, the TN480U is the easier buy.
